metadata.description: The Memphis, Dallas and Gulf (Memphis, Paris and Gulf until 1 Jun 1910), a southwest Arkansas lumber tap line that grew into a Hot Springs - Glenwood - Murfreesboro - Nashville - Ashdown through route (1915-1920, on to Texarkana over the KCS), plus its detached Daleville - Dalark line near Arkadelphia; and its successor on Ashdown - Nashville, the Graysonia, Nashville and Ashdown (1922-1947).
metadata.colour_normalization: Rule 4: both companies are new to data/ (the report's grep and a re-check found no feature for either). Memphis, Dallas and Gulf #5C4B8A (all five MD&G features) and Graysonia, Nashville and Ashdown #3F7F7F; both hexes were checked programmatically to be unused by any other company in data/ and to differ from each other.
metadata.ownership_splits: 1 Jun 1910 Memphis, Paris & Gulf -> Memphis, Dallas & Gulf: a rename of the same corporation, NOT split (the 1908-1910 segment carries the MD&G name and colour; its note says it ran as the MP&G). USRA federal control c.1918 - 1 Mar 1920: not split. 15 Aug 1922 MD&G -> Graysonia, Nashville & Ashdown on Ashdown - Nashville: SPLIT into gna-ashdown-nashville (identical geometry to mdg-ashdown-nashville). 1927 Ideal Cement stock purchase of the GN&A: not split. 1921 Daleville - Dalark lessee (Jas. G. Clark / Hugh T. Ross) under the M.D.G. name: unresolved, not split. Shawmut - Glenwood is Iron Mountain track run by MD&G trains under trackage rights, drawn inside mdg-murfreesboro-glenwood under the MD&G because MD&G ran those trains.
omitted: Block [5] GN&A Nashville - Murfreesboro (1922-1925): drawable NONE - no source that the GN&A carried passengers on this piece.

Block [6] Murfreesboro, Nashville, Southwestern / Murfreesboro and Nashville Railroad Nashville - Murfreesboro (1925-1951/52): drawable NONE - no passenger year sourced; the Feb 1952 Official Guide shows 'FREIGHT SERVICE ONLY' (March 1951); the 1944 POW movement is a one-off government move, not public service.

Block [10] Ultima Thule, Arkadelphia & Mississippi Daleville - Sparkman (Guide listings 1890/1893/1906): omitted by the cycle owner - weak Guide-listing evidence and the company name/years are unresolved.
Block [11] MD&G Dalark - Fairview (1911 anchor): omitted by the cycle owner; only Daleville - Dalark ([12]) is drawn, which carries the same 1911 Tap Line mixed train on its own piece.
Block [13] MD&G Rosboro - Cooper (ex Caddo & Choctaw; 1911 anchor from one Guide station listing): omitted - low confidence.

Freight-only (Rule 1): Antoine Valley / MD&G Graysonia Division Graysonia - Leard (logging trains only); Glenwood, Hot Springs & Western as a Clark Lumber Co. logging road before MD&G acquisition; Caddo & Choctaw under its own name; GN&A Schaal Branch (Schaal - Ramsey - Dodson, no passenger evidence); GN&A after 1947; MN&SW / Murfreesboro & Nashville to 1951-52; Arkansas Southern (Watco) Nashville - Ashdown 2005-.
MD&G through cars Ashdown - Texarkana over the KCS (1918 timetable): KCS track, trackage rights vs connecting service not established; not drawn.
Iron Mountain's own passenger trains on the Gurdon - Glenwood - Norman branch: not part of this layer (st_louis_iron_mountain.geojson has no feature for that branch).
not_yet_sourced: OPEN ENDS: mdg-ashdown-nashville, mdg-nashville-murfreesboro, mdg-murfreesboro-glenwood and mdg-glenwood-hot-springs end at 1920, the last CONFIRMED passenger year (Sept 1920 mixed trains); actual end anywhere 1920 - Aug 1922. mdg-daleville-dalark is [OPEN] at both 1911 and 1921.

GN&A 1922-1947 rests on one secondary source (NR-ASH citing Hull, Shortline Railroads of Arkansas, 1969, pp. 257-305, not online). No GN&A public timetable found; whether passenger service began in 1922 (the motor-car plan) is unverified.
First through train Hot Springs - Texarkana: 3 Mar 1915 (EOA-PIKE) vs 18 Mar 1915 (EOA-MUR).

Routing Glenwood - Shawmut: drawn Glenwood - Amity - Shawmut on the Iron Mountain branch; FOWLER's MD&G sequence lists Rosboro (NW of Glenwood) between Glenwood and Amity, which may mean a reversal via Rosboro or a branch-point indentation - not resolved.

Murfreesboro - Shawmut and Glenwood - Hot Springs are straight-line approximations; the MD&G grades and their intermediate stations (Royston Springs, Stanley, Memdag, Frederick/Schuey etc.) were not located.
1914 Hot Springs terminus: FOWLER puts 1914 service at Schuey (Frederick), 4.5 mi out; the line is drawn to Hot Springs from 1914.
MD&G passenger frequency 1910-1920 beyond the c.1911 Tap Line count and the April 1918 timetable; headway values are estimates.
Who ran Daleville - Dalark in 1921-22 (lessee Jas. G. Clark) and whether FOWLER's 'GNA: Daleville - Dalark' heading reflects a real GN&A operation.
White Cliffs station site: the Nominatim hamlet point is 3.7 km from the drawn pre-relocation grade.

segments.note: Ran under the original name MEMPHIS, PARIS AND GULF (inc. 1906): a Nashville Lumber Co. tap line that carried mail and passengers from the start - passenger equipment arrived by Dec 1907, US Mail inaugurated 13 Apr 1908, Ashdown depot built 1908 'upon the completion of the rail line to Ashdown' (NR-ASH); 'opened for rail traffic in 1907' (NR-MS). 1908 is the first CONFIRMED year (bracket 1907-1910). On 1 Jun 1910 the same corporation was renamed Memphis, Dallas and Gulf - a rename, not an operator change, so it is not split for Rule 4 and the label uses the later name. Headway not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: 1908 start from the Ashdown depot NRHP nomination (mail from 13 Apr 1908, passenger equipment Dec 1907, citing Hull 1969) and the Mineral Springs depot nomination; construction 1906-08 from the ICC valuation; the 1910 rename from the ICC Tap Line case. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Memphis, Dallas and Gulf (renamed 1 Jun 1910, absorbing the Antoine Valley and the Ultima Thule, Arkadelphia & Mississippi). Two passenger-carrying trains daily each way Ashdown - Murfreesboro c.1911 (ICC Tap Line record); from March 1915 part of the Hot Springs - Texarkana through route, which in April 1918 was one train daily except Sunday plus a Sunday-only train (De Queen Bee 19 Apr 1918), running on to Texarkana over the KCS from Ashdown (KCS track, not drawn). USRA federal control c.1918 - 1 Mar 1920 (not split). headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE from the c.1911 two-trains-daily count; by 1918 it was nearer one train a day, and from Sept 1920 three mixed trains a week. END 1920 IS [OPEN]: it is the last CONFIRMED passenger year, not a known end. From 1 Sep 1920 the road ran 'three mixed trains weekly, in each direction', then a crew walkout suspended service indefinitely (De Queen Bee 10 Sep 1920); the Corporation Commission ordered the daily schedule kept pending a hearing whose outcome was not found. The Aug 1922 foreclosure report says service 'during the past year has been practically the same as none'. No source dates when passenger trains actually stopped (bracket 1920 - Aug 1922). Do not extend without evidence.
sources: Segment-level: start from the 1 Jun 1910 rename (ICC Tap Line case, which also gives the c.1911 two-trains-daily count); 1918 service from the De Queen Bee public timetable of 19 Apr 1918; last confirmed service Sept 1920 (De Queen Bee 10 Sep 1920); Aug 1922 'practically the same as none' from the Siftings Herald 16 Aug 1922. End year is [OPEN]. Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: The 'Diamond Line', built 1908-1909 by the Memphis, Paris & Gulf (ICC-MNSW); the 30 Jun 1910 Carlisle Independent says the road 'now extends from Nashville to Murfreesboro' (track, not trains). 1911 is the first CONFIRMED passenger year: the ICC Tap Line record (c.1911) has 'two trains daily in each direction between Ashdown and Murfreesboro on which passengers are carried'. MP&G-era passengers 1909-1910 are plausible but unproven and are not drawn. Prescott & Northwestern trains also used this track Tokio - Nashville under trackage rights c.1911 - P&NW trains, not drawn here. From 1915 part of the Hot Springs - Texarkana through route (De Queen Bee 19 Apr 1918). headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE from the c.1911 count. END 1920 IS [OPEN]: it is the last CONFIRMED passenger year, not a known end. From 1 Sep 1920 the road ran 'three mixed trains weekly, in each direction', then a crew walkout suspended service indefinitely (De Queen Bee 10 Sep 1920); the Corporation Commission ordered the daily schedule kept pending a hearing whose outcome was not found. The Aug 1922 foreclosure report says service 'during the past year has been practically the same as none'. No source dates when passenger trains actually stopped (bracket 1920 - Aug 1922). Do not extend without evidence. Successors on this piece (GN&A 1922-25, Murfreesboro, Nashville, Southwestern from 1925) have no confirmed passenger year and are not drawn.
sources: Segment-level: construction from the ICC valuation (MN&SW); 1911 start from the ICC Tap Line case; 1918 through service from the De Queen Bee timetable; last confirmed service Sept 1920 (De Queen Bee). End year is [OPEN]. Headway is an estimate.

STRAIGHT-LINE LEG: Murfreesboro - Shawmut, 15.3 mi chord against ~19 mi documented - the MD&G's own grade (via Royston Springs, Stephenson, Stanley, Rabell, Wright, Anderson; rails up by 1926) is absent from OSM (abandoned/razed/demolished queried directly), OSM rail-trails and OpenHistoricalMap, and none of those intermediate stations could be geocoded in Arkansas. Shawmut WAS located: Nominatim locality 'Shawmut, Pike County' (34.152 N, 93.450 W), on the Gurdon branch 0.0 km from the drawn line, about 7.9 mi south of Amity (FOWLER: 9.3 mi). TRACED, IRON MOUNTAIN TRACK: Shawmut - Amity - Glenwood, 17.2 mi on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=MP (railway=disused/abandoned, ex Gurdon & Fort Smith, later Caddo Valley RR), 0.1 mi connector; Amity 1.0 km, Glenwood 0.2 km from the line. This leg is St. Louis, Iron Mountain & Southern / Missouri Pacific property used by MD&G trains under trackage rights, drawn here because MD&G ran the trains. Drawn on the alignment that survives in OSM; whether it matches the 1915 alignment was not checked. Rosboro (FOWLER mp 38.9, NW of Glenwood) is not on the drawn line - see not_yet_sourced.

segments.note: The middle of the Hot Springs - Texarkana through route. Murfreesboro - Shawmut (~19 mi) was MD&G's own line: track-laying began at Murfreesboro 7 May 1913 (EOA-MUR) and the 'last link of the Hot Springs-Texarkana line' was 'ready for the operation of trains' by 25 Mar 1915 (Carlisle Independent). First through train 3 Mar 1915 (EOA-PIKE) vs 18 Mar 1915 (EOA-MUR) - CONFLICT recorded, both 1915. Shawmut - Amity - Glenwood (~17.6 mi) was NOT MD&G property: MD&G trains ran over the St. Louis, Iron Mountain & Southern's Gurdon - Norman branch (ex Gurdon & Fort Smith) - the Aug 1922 foreclosure sale lists MD&G property only 'Ashdown to Shawmut and from Glenwood to Hot Springs', and NR-ASH describes 'passage over the intersecting rails of the Gurdon & Ft. Smith'. The Iron Mountain's own trains on that branch are not drawn here. headway_min 1440 is an ESTIMATE from the April 1918 timetable (one through train daily except Sunday each way, plus a Sunday train). The ICC let the receivers discontinue 'Shawmut and Nashville' on 18 Jul 1922 and rails north of Murfreesboro were up by 1926 - abandonment dates, not passenger ends. END 1920 IS [OPEN]: it is the last CONFIRMED passenger year, not a known end. From 1 Sep 1920 the road ran 'three mixed trains weekly, in each direction', then a crew walkout suspended service indefinitely (De Queen Bee 10 Sep 1920); the Corporation Commission ordered the daily schedule kept pending a hearing whose outcome was not found. The Aug 1922 foreclosure report says service 'during the past year has been practically the same as none'. No source dates when passenger trains actually stopped (bracket 1920 - Aug 1922). Do not extend without evidence.
sources: Segment-level: 1915 start from EOA-MUR, EOA-PIKE (conflicting March dates) and the Carlisle Independent of 25 Mar 1915; 1918 service from the De Queen Bee timetable; last confirmed service Sept 1920 (De Queen Bee); trackage-rights status of Shawmut - Glenwood from the Siftings Herald sale notice of 16 Aug 1922 and NR-ASH; ICC discontinuance from the Siftings Herald of 18 Jul 1922. End year is [OPEN]. Headway is an estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: ENTIRELY STRAIGHT-LINE: 30.9 mi drawn vs 35.1 mi documented (FOWLER mp 0.0 Hot Springs - 35.1 Glenwood). Four chords through geocoded places: Glenwood - Bonnerdale 10.5 mi, Bonnerdale - Pearcy 6.1 mi, Pearcy - Hempwallace 4.6 mi, Hempwallace - Hot Springs 9.8 mi. The MD&G / Glenwood, Hot Springs & Western grade (junked after Dec 1922) is absent from OSM (abandoned/razed/demolished queried directly, rail-trails) and OpenHistoricalMap; the MP-tagged abandoned grade leaving Glenwood is the Iron Mountain's Norman branch, NOT this line, and was not used. Bonnerdale stands in for Memdag (EoA: Memdag was in the later Bonnerdale area); Lucky, Imelda, Clark Junction, Milton and Frederick (Schuey) could not be geocoded. Hot Springs end is the city centroid, not a sourced MD&G depot site. The whole line is drawn from 1914 although the 1914 terminus was Schuey (Frederick), 4.5 mi short of Hot Springs.

segments.note: Built partly on the former Glenwood, Hot Springs & Western logging road (~20 mi, acquired c.1911-12; its logging-era operation is not drawn). The MD&G's 'initial train' into Hot Springs was to be christened 17 Mar 1914 (Forrest City Times 13 Mar 1914), and FOWLER shows Schuey (later Frederick, mp 4.5) as the terminus of service in the 1914 Official Guide - so in 1914 trains may have stopped 4.5 mi short of Hot Springs; the whole line is drawn from 1914 regardless. From March 1915 part of the Hot Springs - Texarkana through route (one train daily except Sunday each way plus a Sunday train, De Queen Bee 19 Apr 1918); headway_min 1440 is an ESTIMATE from that timetable. FOWLER's 'East Spur 1923G pass?' is a 1923 listing he himself questions and is not treated as evidence of 1923 service. The ICC authorised discontinuance 18 Jul 1922 and the Arkansas Railroad Commission let the line be junked in Dec 1922 - abandonment dates, not passenger ends. END 1920 IS [OPEN]: it is the last CONFIRMED passenger year, not a known end. From 1 Sep 1920 the road ran 'three mixed trains weekly, in each direction', then a crew walkout suspended service indefinitely (De Queen Bee 10 Sep 1920); the Corporation Commission ordered the daily schedule kept pending a hearing whose outcome was not found. The Aug 1922 foreclosure report says service 'during the past year has been practically the same as none'. No source dates when passenger trains actually stopped (bracket 1920 - Aug 1922). Do not extend without evidence.
sources: Segment-level: 1914 start from the Forrest City Times of 13 Mar 1914 and FOWLER's 1914 Guide note; 1918 service from the De Queen Bee timetable; last confirmed service Sept 1920 (De Queen Bee); junking from the Siftings Herald of 22 Dec 1922; GHS&W acquisition from the ICC Tap Line case. End year is [OPEN]. Headway is an estimate.

properties.line: Graysonia, Nashville and Ashdown: Ashdown – Nashville
properties.speed_source: estimated: no GN&A public timetable was found; 25 km/h is a guess for a 27-mile lumber/cement short line and is NOT sourced.

Douglas-Peucker 8 m, reversals trimmed; no out-and-back spurs.

Operator split: 26.2 mi on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator='Graysonia, Nashville and Ashdown', 0.2 mi untagged yard track at the ends. PRE-RELOCATION ALIGNMENT: Ashdown - Schaal - Mineral Springs is drawn on OSM way 165858951 (railway=abandoned, old_railway_operator='Graysonia, Nashville and Ashdown', 18.7 mi), the pre-Millwood Lake grade; the post-1960s relocation via Okay that today's Arkansas Southern 'Southern Branch' follows was NOT used. Mineral Springs - Nashville is today's Arkansas Southern track (same GN&A tag), assumed unchanged since 1908, and the GN&A ran on the pre-relocation grade throughout 1922-1947 (Millwood Lake was impounded in the 1960s) - not checked against a pre-1960 map. Waypoints: Ashdown 0.0, Schaal 0.1, Mineral Springs 0.4, Nashville 0.2 km from the line; White Cliffs (Nominatim hamlet) lies 3.7 km off the drawn grade - the station may have stood away from today's hamlet point, not verified. segments.note: Graysonia, Nashville & Ashdown Railroad, incorporated 25 Oct 1922 to take Ashdown - Nashville (and, to Jan 1925, Nashville - Murfreesboro, not drawn) after the MD&G foreclosure sale of 15 Aug 1922; GN&A on its own account from 1 Sep 1922 (ICC-GNA). LOW CONFIDENCE, SINGLE SECONDARY SOURCE: the only positive statement of passenger service for the whole span is the 1994 Ashdown depot NRHP nomination, relying on Hull (1969): 'Ideal transformed the GN & A into a freight operation by and large, though the company continued to offer passenger service until 1947'. Passenger service in 1922 itself is unproven - the purchaser only 'proposes to put on motor cars for passenger, mail and baggage service' (Siftings Herald 16 Aug 1922), a plan. No GN&A public timetable, mixed-train notice or last-train story was found; a 19 May 1923 item mentions 'the Graysonia, Nashville & Ashdown train' but not that it carried passengers. Ideal Cement's 1927 stock purchase did not change who ran the trains (not split). The Feb 1952 Official Guide (Aug 1951 schedule) lists the GN&A as 'Operated for Freight, Mail and Express only', consistent with the 1947 end. Freight continued (KCS from 1993, then Arkansas Southern) - context only. Headway not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: SINGLE SECONDARY SOURCE - span from the Ashdown depot NRHP nomination ('passenger service until 1947', citing Hull, Shortline Railroads of Arkansas, 1969); operator change from the ICC valuation; 1922 plan from the Siftings Herald of 16 Aug 1922; freight-only by 1951 from the Feb 1952 Official Guide. No primary source confirms any year 1922-1947. Headway not sourced.

properties.line: Memphis, Dallas and Gulf: Daleville – Dalark
properties.speed_source: estimated: 15 km/h is a guess for a daily mixed train on a lumber tap line; no timetable times were read. NOT sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: 10.7 mi drawn vs about 12 mi documented (FOWLER s.112). Traced 7.1 mi on untagged OSM railway=abandoned ways 1022918685 / 1022917716 (east of Daleville toward Dalark) plus 1.4 mi on way 1022917717 into Dalark. STRAIGHT-LINE LEGS: Daleville - start of surviving grade 1.5 mi, a 0.6 mi gap between the two abandoned ways, and no leg into the Dalark hamlet point: the grade is drawn to its end ~0.15 mi east of it (a 0.2 mi chord back west to the point was removed as a reversal hook). The abandoned ways are untagged for operator; their attribution to the ex-Ultima Thule / MD&G Arkadelphia Division rests on position (no other railway ran Daleville - Dalark). Tupelo, Bobo and Haygood could not be geocoded (Nominatim returned a Tupelo in Jackson County). OpenHistoricalMap had nothing.

segments.note: MD&G Arkadelphia Division, the surviving west end of the former Ultima Thule, Arkadelphia & Mississippi (Grayson-McLeod lumber road), taken over 1 Jun 1910. START 1911 IS [OPEN]: it is the ICC Tap Line record year - 'A single "mixed train" is operated daily' over Daleville - Fairview, few passengers; mixed trains count as passenger service. Earlier MD&G years (1910) and the UTA&M's own-name years are not drawn. END 1921 IS [OPEN]: 'The M. D. G. Railroad will resume operations Saturday ... four runs a week ... ready to accept freight and passengers', Daleville - Dalark (Siftings Herald 10 Mar 1921); by 3 Aug 1921 the road was run by 'Jas. G. Clark ... lessee' under the MD&G name - operator identity unresolved, not split. The 'Daleville branch' was in the Aug 1922 foreclosure sale; nothing confirms passengers in 1922 or later. Do not extend either end without evidence. headway_min 1440 is an ESTIMATE from the 1911 daily mixed train (four runs a week in 1921).
sources: Segment-level: 1911 daily mixed train from the ICC Tap Line case; 1921 passenger resumption and lessee from the Siftings Herald of 10 Mar and 3 Aug 1921; route and stations from FOWLER s.112. Both ends are [OPEN]. Headway is an estimate.
